title: latexmk: command not found on Mac (BasicTeX fix)
short_title: latexmk: command not found? Two commands fix it

runs.output:

verify.notes: Packages latexmk and biber exist in TeX Live 2026 (tlmgr info). BasicTeX installs into a root-owned tree, so its tlmgr needs sudo; the fix Ben gave a customer on 2026-10-14 worked.

scenes.title: latexmk: command not found
scenes.sub: The build stops before it starts.
scenes.narration: If your LaTeX build on a Mac stops with latexmk: command not found, or biber: command not found, here is the fix.

scenes.label: Terminal
scenes.narration: This is what it looks like in Terminal. In VS Code, LaTeX Workshop reports the same thing as spawn latexmk E N O E N T.

scenes.text: BasicTeX is the small version of MacTeX. It leaves out latexmk and biber.
scenes.narration: BasicTeX is the small version of MacTeX. It leaves out latexmk and biber, the two tools most editors call to build a document and its bibliography.

scenes.label: Terminal
scenes.ui: BasicTeX's files belong to the system, so each command asks for your Mac password.
scenes.narration: Open Terminal. Update the package manager first, then install both tools. BasicTeX's files belong to the system, so each command needs sudo and your Mac password.

scenes.label: Terminal
scenes.narration: Check both. If each prints a version, open a new Terminal window or restart your editor, and build again.

scenes.name: ModernTex
scenes.line: Uses the TeX installation that has everything a build needs, and installs a missing package for you.
scenes.narration: If you write LaTeX on a Mac, ModernTex picks the TeX installation that has everything a build needs, and installs a missing package for you. There is a free seven day trial.
